Baby Greens Salad

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 4Prep 15 min

Baby Greens Salad is a fresh, vibrant dish traditionally served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet, which commemorates the children martyred in Bethlehem. This simple yet elegant salad symbolizes innocence and purity, making it a fitting accompaniment to the solemn yet hopeful occasion.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups mixed baby greens (about 120 g)
  • 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, halved (about 75 g)
  • 1/4 cup thinly sliced red onion (about 30 g)
  • 1/4 cup crumbled feta cheese (about 35 g)
  • 1/4 cup toasted walnuts, chopped (about 30 g)
  • 3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (45 ml)
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice (15 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon honey (5 ml)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Method

  1. In a large salad bowl, combine the baby greens, cherry tomatoes, and sliced red onion.
  2. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, honey, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
  3. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
  4. Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese and toasted walnuts over the top before serving.

Tips

  • Use a variety of baby greens such as spinach, arugula, and baby kale for more texture and flavor.
  • For a nut-free version, substitute walnuts with toasted pumpkin seeds or omit entirely.
  • Add thinly sliced cucumber or radishes for extra crunch and freshness.
